scope: Proposition D.6 (The global shielding output) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-codimension-two-width-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f67c30579306bd4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 82. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At a fixed stage r, let j0 be the current label and keep its true minimizers fixed. There are updates of every remaining profile and core, and compatible smooth additions Dj ≥ 0, with the following properties on every parent packet E of dimension m: (i) The updated profiles have locally Lipschitz finite truncations and satisfy, almost everywhere on their finite bands, 2|∇µ′ j| ≤ ar(µ′ j)2 + Πj + Dj. (D.14) All these data are exact compatible products. Each core only enlarges, and its closure remains in the interior of its designated updated pole set. The original forced sets and the anchor sign restrictions are preserved. (ii) With G′ j = E \ (U′+ j ∪ U′− j ), the set H∗ E = n x : #{j ̸= j0 : x ∈ G′ j} ≥ m − 2 o (D.15) is closed and misses ΣE. In an exact collar over a face B, its projection is contained in H∗ B. This holds for every further face and every simultaneous product limit. (iii) For one common θ∗ < .9, all walls and joined sides satisfy Z 1.16 X j̸=j0 Djv2 ≤ θ∗ N(v) + e0∥v∥2 2  ≤ .9 N(v) + e0∥v∥2 2  . (D.16) The additions are bounded with their derivatives on each post-radial packet. There are only finitely many local additions on each such packet and only finitely many extensions into it. For the initial radial parent the same conclusions hold with locally finite additions over its compact transition shells; boundedness is asserted on the corresponding compact blocks and Equation (D.16) holds on every compact test. No convergence assertion at an end of the original manifold is needed.
